questions.question: Define orthonasal smelling. Describe its role in odour perception / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Define orthonasal smelling. Describe its role in odour perception.
  • Orthonasal smelling is the perception of odours when volatile compounds enter the nose through
  • the nostrils during inhalation.
  • Role in odour perception:
  • • It helps detect the aroma of food before it is eaten.
  • • It plays an important role in identifying food quality and freshness.
  • • It contributes to flavour perception along with taste.
  • • It influences appetite and food acceptance.
  • • It helps in detecting spoilage or undesirable odours in food.

questions.question: Discuss on mean and median with suitable examples / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss mean and median with suitable examples.
  • Mean:
  • Mean is the average value of a set of numbers. It is calculated by dividing the sum of all
  • observations by the total number of observations.
  • Formula:
  • Mean = (Sum of observations) / (Number of observations)
  • Example:
  • Scores given by panelists for sweetness: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10
  • Mean = (6 + 7 + 8 + 9 + 10) / 5 = 40 / 5 = 8
  • Median:
  • Median is the middle value in a set of observations arranged in ascending or descending order.
  • Example:
  • Scores: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11
  • The middle value is 7, so the median is 7.
  • Mean represents the average value, while median represents the central value of the data.

questions.question: List and describe the five basic tastes. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• List and describe the five basic tastes.
  • The five basic tastes are sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami. Sweet taste is usually
  • produced by sugars such as glucose and sucrose and is generally pleasant, indicating the
  • presence of energy -rich carbohydrates. Sour taste is caused by acids such as ci tric acid or
  • acetic acid and gives a sharp or tangy sensation, commonly found in foods like lemon and
  • vinegar. Salty taste is mainly produced by mineral salts, especially sodium chloride, and is
  • important for maintaining electrolyte balance and enhancing f lavor in foods. Bitter taste is
  • caused by substances such as caffeine, quinine, and certain plant compounds; it is often
  • considered unpleasant and may act as a warning signal for toxic substances. Umami taste is
  • a savory taste produced by compounds such as monosodium glutamate (MSG) and
  • naturally occurring glutamates in foods like meat, mushrooms, and cheese, giving a rich
  • and meaty flavor.

questions.question: Identify the seven types of rating tests used in sensory evaluation and explain any four. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Identify the seven types of rating tests used in sensory evaluation and explain any four.
  • Rating tests are used in sensory evaluation to measure the intensity or quality of sensory
  • attributes of food products. The seven types of rating tests commonly used are numerical
  • scale rating test, graphic rating test, category scale test, hedonic rating test, ranking test,
  • paired comparison test, and composite scoring test.
  • The numerical scale rating test uses numbers, usually from 1 to 9 or 1 to 10, to rate the
  • intensity or quality of a sensory attribute such as sweetness or texture. In the graphic rating
  • test, panelists mark their response on a line between two extremes, such as “very poor” and
  • “excellent,” to indicate the intensity of a characteristic. The category scale test provides
  • specific categories such as poor, fair, good, very good, and excellent, and panelists select
  • the category that best represents the sample. The hedonic rating test measures the degree of
  • liking or preference of a product, commonly using a 9 -point hedonic scale ranging from
  • “dislike extremely” to “like extremely.” These tests help researchers evalua te consumer
  • acceptance and sensory quality of food products.

questions.question: Explain the importance of texture in processed foods. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the importance of texture in processed foods.
  • Texture is an important sensory attribute that refers to the physical feel and structure of
  • food when it is handled or eaten. It includes characteristics such as hardness, softness,
  • crispness, chewiness, and smoothness. In processed foods, texture plays a major role in
  • determining consumer acceptance and overall product quality. A desirable texture
  • enhances the eating experience and contributes to the perception of freshness and quality.
  • For example, crispness is expected in chips, softness in bread, and creaminess in dairy
  • products. Improper processing, storage, or formulation can negatively affect texture,
  • leading to undesirable ch aracteristics such as staleness or toughness. Therefore,
  • maintaining the appropriate texture during processing and storage is essential for the
  • success of processed food products.

questions.question: Discuss the steps involved in recruiting sensory panel members for a laboratory. / [CO2] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the steps involved in recruiting sensory panel members for a laboratory.
  • Recruiting sensory panel members is an important step in conducting accurate sensory
  • evaluation. The first step is identifying the need for panelists based on the type of sensory
  • test and the number of participants required. The next step is advertising or inviting
  • volunteers from students, staff, or the general public who are interested in participating in
  • sensory testing. After this, screening tests are conducted to evaluate the sensory ability of
  • the candidates, including their ability to detect basic tastes, odors, and differences between
  • samples. Candidates who perform well in these tests are selected for the panel. The
  • selected individuals then undergo training sessions to familiarize them with sensory
  • attributes, evaluation procedures, and th e use of scorecards or scales. During training,
  • panelists also learn how to avoid bias and maintain consistency in evaluation. Finally, the
  • trained panelists are organized into a sensory panel and are regularly monitored and
  • evaluated to maintain their per formance and reliability in sensory testing. Proper
  • recruitment and training ensure accurate and reliable sensory evaluation results.
